answer: Each identity must complete a long chain of sequential modular squarings before producing its Wesolowski proof; later steps depend on earlier results, so GPUs cannot parallelize away the latency of any one chain. An attacker may run clone chains concurrently, but each demands its own sustained computation, making Sybil identities costly in physical time and resources. Like a jetty facing an ocean, the beacon marks progress, not a shortcut.
